newsitem.title: CHINA: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - FITIC DEAL SHOULD FIT.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - FITIC DEAL SHOULD FIT.

text.p: HONG KONG, Aug 7 (Reuter - Fujian International Trust and Investment Corp (FITIC) is expected imminently with its US$100 million 10-year 144a, bankers said on Thursday.
"I think it'll go fine," said one investment banker, who, however, thought an expected spread of about 100 basis points over U.S. treasuries was a little tight.
Bankers said the pricing seemed close to that of Hutchison Whampoa's recent deal given their different ratings.
FITIC is rated BBB by Standard & Poor's (S&P) against Hutchison Whampoa Ltd, which S&P rates A-plus.
Hutchison's recent global bond saw the 10-year tranche go at a spread of 82 basis points over U.S. treasuries.
However, bankers said China was popular at the moment, and expected the deal to fly.
In other news, Alphatec Electronics Plc, an early victim of Thailand's economic woes, has won a reprieve.
Bondholders decided to give it one month to present restructuring plans, Alphatec told Reuters on Thursday, after a bondholders' meeting in Zurich on Wednesday.
Bond trustee Bankers Trust called the meeting after Alphatec failed to pay bondholders who exercised a put option on a US$45 million euroconvertible bond.
Alphatec will meet bondholders around September 5.
In other news, Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corp issued HK$3.5 billion in three-year floating-rate certificate of deposits (FRCDs).
However, arranger HSBC Markets ended up with almost half of the issue, taking HK$1.7 billion.
Some bankers who turned down the paper said they would have preferred an all-in yield of 30 basis points to the 27 basis points all-in that was offered.
"You're being asked to take HK$200 million (to join the deal) -- it's a big chunk of money," one banker commented.
"There's a lot of (HongkongBank) paper around," he added.
This is the sixth issue by HongkongBank to be eligible for the liquidity adjustment facility operated by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, and all were for more than HK$1 billion.
HongkongBank said it increased the size of its certificate of deposit programme by 50 percent to HK$30 billion to accommodate the size of the latest issue.
The CD programme now has 49 individual issues totalling more than HK$23 billion.
HongkongBank said it was its first certificate of deposit issue to be done bond-style.

Another cross-border asset-backed securitisation could be on the cards in the territory, with Belgian Bank confirming that it is talking to HSBC Markets, arranger of the successful US$300 million deal for Dah Sing Bank Ltd in June.
Recent cross-border packaging of Hong Kong loans have highlighted investor appetite for the securities.
